title: Palo Alto Networks: sideloaded fake "Google Chrome" extension steals Microsoft and Google cookies and streams webcam feeds
date_note: Date is the publication day of the Palo Alto Networks report; the page gives no earlier day for the finding.
geo_basis: No victim location is stated for the extension; pin placed on the researcher (Palo Alto Networks, Santa Clara, USA)
summary: Palo Alto Networks researchers describe a malicious extension named "Google Chrome" that was not on the Chrome Web Store and that victims had to sideload using Developer Mode from oskeysetup[.]com. They say it harvests Microsoft and Google authentication cookies, installs keyloggers and streams webcam feeds. They assess with moderate confidence that attackers associated with CL-CRI-1192 (Helix) developed it.
plain: Palo Alto Networks describes a fake "Google Chrome" extension that victims had to install by hand. It harvests Microsoft and Google sign-in cookies, logs keystrokes and streams webcam feeds, the researchers say.
exec: Palo Alto Networks research shows a sideloaded extension that harvests session cookies for Microsoft and Google accounts.
action: Palo Alto Networks advises browser extension allowlists, phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkeys) and tighter help desk verification.

validation.note: Primary: Palo Alto Networks report read directly; Cyber Press and GBHackers relay it. Attribution is Unit 42's moderate-confidence assessment only.

review.note: sectors: was unknown/inferred; GBHackers states organisations holding financial and healthcare data are targeted, now financial-services and healthcare-public-health, stated. Title, date, capabilities, Helix moderate-confidence attribution, action and single_source checked against GBHackers.
